transcript.text: Good morning everyone. As you know, we're under a 48-hour water conservation restriction from the municipal authority, and I need to finalize our water-control plan. Before I sign off, I'd like to hear the updates from Quality, Maintenance, and EHS as per our routine conservation huddle. We've got 2,400 liters of reclaimed water available, and both Line X and Line Y are scheduled to run during the restriction. Let's start with Quality — what's your update?

transcript.text: I have a lab test completed this morning that hasn't been uploaded to the shared quality folder yet. The reclaimed-water conductivity came in at 1,800 microsiemens per centimeter. Line X's process limit is 1,200, so reclaimed water is NOT acceptable for Line X. Line Y's process limit is 2,200, and Line Y's scheduled batch requires exactly 1,800 liters, so reclaimed water is acceptable for Line Y — but only after a conductivity test is recorded.

transcript.text: I have an update from Maintenance. My inspection of the recovery skid — documented in my maintenance notebook but not yet entered in the work-order system — found that the skid requires an exact 3-hour membrane flush before use, and after that flush it can deliver reclaimed water at no more than 600 liters per hour. That's important for planning: to supply Line Y's 1,800-liter batch requirement, the skid would need to run for 3 hours of flushing plus 3 hours of delivery time at 600 liters per hour.

transcript.text: I have an update from EHS. During my permit review with the municipal inspector yesterday — the review is awaiting attachment to the site's permit record — I found that reclaimed water may be used only after its residual sanitizer is adjusted to exactly 0.3 parts per million, and that each use day requires a signed sanitizer log. So before we commit to using reclaimed water on Line Y, we need to ensure the sanitizer level is adjusted to 0.3 ppm and that the sanitizer log is signed for each day of use.

decisions.reclaimed_water_plan: Use reclaimed water for Line Y only. Line X must not use reclaimed water due to conductivity exceeding its process limit. Line Y's batch requires 1,800 liters, which is within the 2,400-liter available supply and below Line Y's conductivity limit of 2,200. The recovery skid must undergo a 3-hour membrane flush before delivering water at 600 liters/hour for 3 hours to supply the 1,800-liter batch. Sanitizer must be adjusted to 0.3 ppm and the sanitizer log signed for each day of use. A conductivity test must be recorded before Line Y uses the reclaimed water.

commitments.detail: Upload the reclaimed-water conductivity test result (1,800 µS/cm) to the shared quality folder and record it before Line Y begins using reclaimed water.
Enter the recovery skid inspection findings into the work-order system and schedule the 3-hour membrane flush followed by 3 hours of delivery at 600 liters/hour to supply Line Y's 1,800-liter batch.
Attach the municipal permit review to the site's permit record, ensure sanitizer is adjusted to 0.3 ppm, and sign the sanitizer log for each day of reclaimed-water use on Line Y.
